facts.text: North Melbourne was originally called Hotham, named after Governor Charles Hotham, before being renamed on 26 August 1887.
The Metropolitan Meat Market, built in 1901, once sold meat and flowers and now stands as a heritage landmark.
The suburb’s first town hall and meat market were designed by architect George Raymond Johnson, a key figure in Victorian architecture.
North Melbourne’s tram network began in the 1890s, with route 57 still running down Flemington Road to Flinders Street.
In the 1990s many old factories and warehouses were converted into fashionable loft‑style apartments, reshaping the suburb’s skyline.
North Melbourne’s boundaries are defined by CityLink freeway to the west, Victoria Street to the south, O'Connell and Peel Streets to the east, and Flemington Road to the north.
